functionalReqs: Consumer groups read messages; each message goes to one consumer per group
Messages retained for a configurable period and replayable
hints: Why is an append-only log on disk fast? What does sequential I/O buy you?
Split topics into partitions spread over brokers; consumers track offsets. How is a partition replicated?

Partition leader plus followers (ISR), producer acks (0/1/all), segment files with an index, batching and zero-copy, offsets committed per consumer group, a controller (ZooKeeper or Raft-based) for metadata and leader election, and rebalancing consumer groups.
nonFunctionalReqs: Durable: no loss after an acknowledged write
problemStatement:
Design a **distributed message queue** like Kafka: producers publish messages to topics; consumer groups read them in order, at their own pace, and can replay.

Throughput, durability and ordering are the main concerns.
title: Design a Distributed Message Queue (Kafka)
